name: MureDistribution trusts the caller-supplied pool source for the claim signer
summary: MureDistribution.distribute takes the pool source, repository and amount from the caller and checks the claim signature against source.poolState(pool).signer, so any contract implementing PoolMetadata can name itself signer and approve its own ERC-1271 claim. The attacker's contract did so and pulled 4,848,684 QUEST from the project's distribution repository 0x29b0a315, which had approved the proxy, and sold them for 5.45 ETH; two copycats first released 282,151 vested QUEST from 0x7c01aa37 into the repository and took them the same way.
notes: The proxy has run 0xec9c8e3b since its creation, which set the route; the next upgrade (0xc35c629d, block 25179281) came after the exploit.
Campaign: every Distribution event of the proxy; the 165 before the anchor all name the project's pool source 0xed1583b9, and the three after it name attacker contracts.

QUEST is valued at realised proceeds (rule 12): the anchor's sale lowered the QUEST/USDC pool 0x31a43eb4 price from 0.00301278 to 0.00197288 USDC per QUEST, about 35%. The anchor and the copycats' disposal transactions 0x116717c7 and 0x557f58d9 realised 11702.884506, 584.181195 and 236.726250 USDC respectively, before further conversion to ETH. Their 12523.791951 USDC total is $12519.63 at each sale's DefiLlama quote (loss.mjs on the pool's USDC outflows); the disposal transactions are refs, not further exploits.
